subject: Clarifying deployment boundaries and dataflow matrix for private install

Subject: HealthCore RFP: private deployment clarifications needed

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the initial materials — the board wants a short annex that spells out what components in a private deployment can and cannot egress to the public internet, and a clear dataflow map for PII and PHI. Can you provide a matrix that lists:

- runtime components (front-end API, router/proxy, inference workers, KV cache, metrics/telemetry)
- whether each component requires outbound access, and to which endpoints
- required ports and firewall rules for onsite connectivity
- recommended KMS/HSM configuration for key material used by the models

We are on a tight timeline (internal security review next Friday). A simple spreadsheet + annotated diagram would do.

Best,
Maria

Subject: Re: HealthCore RFP: private deployment clarifications needed

Maria — please find our deliverables attached and summarized below. We focused on minimal egress and clear separation of data planes for PHI-sensitive workloads.

Attachments (zipped in email):
- deployment-boundaries-matrix.xlsx (tabbed: components, egress, ports, KMS, patching)
- dataflow-diagram.png (annotated sequence flows, ingress/egress arrows)
- airgap-checklist.pdf (practical steps for air-gapped installs and offline upgrades)

Executive summary (high level):
- Isolation model: Customers can choose one of two private modes: VPC-private (control plane in customer VPC with strict egress policies) or Air-gapped (no outbound connection from compute plane; control plane via one-way import/export media).
- Egress requirements: Only the optional control-plane sync and license checks require outbound access in VPC-private; these can be pinned to fixed IP ranges and TTLs. In air-gapped mode, no outbound egress is required.
- KMS/HSM: We support integration with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11). Key wrapping is enforced for model encryption keys; private keys are never exported by our agent.
- Telemetry/logging: All inference logs and traces can be configured to stay on-prem; if you opt to push to a cloud bucket for aggregated analytics we recommend signed, short-lived upload tokens with strict RBAC.
- Patch/upgrade path: For air-gapped installs we provide signed artifact bundles and an offline apply tool. Rollback is supported via snapshotting worker containers and KV cache checkpoints. See airgap-checklist.pdf for a step-by-step flow.
- Ports & firewall: Minimal inbound required is the customer-managed load balancer to edge proxy. Internal worker-to-worker communication uses ephemeral ports; we list recommended firewall policies in the matrix.

Selected technical notes (excerpts from matrix):
1) Inference workers: no external DNS resolution required in air-gap; for VPC-private, allow outbound to our control-plane IPs (tcp 443) and NTP (udp 123) is optional but recommended.
2) KV cache (optional): can be deployed on local persistent disks; no egress; backup uploads use customer-controlled storage endpoints.
3) Model updates: delivered as signed artifacts. SHA256 checks and signature verification mandatory for air-gapped installs.
4) Audit logs: we provide an audit bundle with tamper-evident sequence numbers; retention policy is customer-configurable.

Open items for HealthCore to confirm:
- Desired retention period for raw inference logs (default 90 days if not specified)
- If you require HSM-backed TLS for service certificates (we currently support this as an opt-in)

If helpful, Marcus and I can join your security review next Friday to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Technical Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: deployment-boundaries-matrix.xlsx, dataflow-diagram.png, airgap-checklist.pdf

Vanessa — this is excellent, thank you. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize the annex:

- Can you confirm the rollback window and behavioral fallback if a model artifact fails signature verification during an air-gapped upgrade? We need language on automatic fallbacks to last-known-good artifacts.
- For the telemetry push option, can you enumerate the auth patterns supported (S3 presigned, OAuth2 client creds, signed upload tokens)? Our compliance team prefers token-based uploads scoped to a single bucket.

I'll coordinate internally and circle back with a short list of retention numbers and whether HSM-backed TLS is required. If you and Marcus are available, please put the security review on your calendars for Fri 03/31 at 09:30 PST.

Warm regards,
Maria
